description:
The Bishop's Palace of Porto, also called the Episcopal Palace (Paço Episcopal do Porto), stands beside Porto Cathedral (Sé) on the Terreiro da Sé, in the historic centre of the city. The present palace is essentially the work of Bishop D. Frei João Rafael de Mendonça (1771–1793), and its façade is often associated with the influence of Nicolau Nasoni. There has been a bishop's residence beside the Cathedral since at least Bishop D. Hugo (1112/1114–1136), and a late-Romanesque window of the 13th century survives to the right of the main door.

Inside, the visit takes in the monumental neoclassical staircase, with mural painting and flowers carved in granite; palatial salons hung with portraits of the Bishops of Porto, including works by Henrique Medina and Júlio Resende; and the recreated dining room of the 3rd Viscounts of São João da Pesqueira, with the “Baixela Manuelina” silver service designed by Rafael Bordalo Pinheiro and made by Reis & Filhos. The visit ends with views over the Douro.

Today the palace is the official residence of the bishops and the administrative seat of the diocese, and since 2016 it has had a museum space. It is open every day with a break at midday, and the visit takes 45 minutes to 1 hour. The Terreiro da Sé in front of the Cathedral and palace can be visited freely and looks south over the Ribeira rooftops to the Douro.
history:
There has been an episcopal residence beside Porto Cathedral since at least Bishop D. Hugo (1112/1114–1136), and a late-Romanesque window of the 13th century survives to the right of the main door of the present building. The present palace is essentially the work of Bishop D. Frei João Rafael de Mendonça (1771–1793); its façade is often associated with the influence of Nicolau Nasoni.

The works were interrupted by the French occupation of 1809 and by the civil war. The Siege of Porto (1832–1833) badly damaged the building, which was rebuilt from 1868 and completed in 1871.

The palace has been a National Monument since 1910, and between 1916 and 1957 it was the seat of Porto's city council. Today it is the official residence of the bishops and the administrative seat of the diocese, and since 2016 it has had a museum space.
how_to_visit:
**Getting there:** The Bishop's Palace is on the Terreiro da Sé, directly beside Porto Cathedral, in the historic Sé neighbourhood. It is a 10-minute walk uphill from São Bento railway station, well served by the Porto Metro (São Bento stop, lines A/B/C/E/F) and the city's historic tram network. No parking at the site; Porto's historic centre is best explored on foot.

**Tickets:** Tickets are sold at the entrance; admission is a few euros, and older listings show around €5. Ask at the desk about the combined ticket with the Cathedral. You can also book a guided tour of about 1 hour online through the GetYourGuide link on this page, from €15, with instant confirmation and cancellation available.

**The view from the Terreiro da Sé:** The terrace in front of the cathedral and palace can be visited freely, and looks south over the Ribeira rooftops to the Douro and across to the port wine lodges of Vila Nova de Gaia.

**Practical tips:** Allow 45 minutes to 1 hour for the visit. The palace is open every day with a break at midday; see the opening hours in the FAQ below.

**Combine with:** [Palácio da Bolsa](/castles/portugal/palacio-da-bolsa), about 400 m to the west; Porto Cathedral, which adjoins the palace; the Ribeira district, reached by the steep lanes from the cathedral hill down to the riverfront; and the Dom Luís I Bridge, with the port wine lodges of Vila Nova de Gaia on the opposite bank.

faqs.question: What are the Bishop's Palace Porto opening hours?
faqs.answer: The palace is open every day, Monday to Sunday, with a break at midday, according to the Diocese of Porto's website. In winter it opens 09:00–13:30 and 14:00–17:30, with last entries at 13:00 and 17:00. In summer it opens 09:00–13:00 and 14:00–18:00, with last entries at 12:30 and 17:30. Allow 45 minutes to 1 hour for the visit.

faqs.answer: Tickets are sold at the entrance; admission is a few euros, and older listings show around €5. Ask at the desk about the combined ticket with the Cathedral. You can also book a guided tour of about 1 hour online through the GetYourGuide link on this page, from €15, with instant confirmation and cancellation available.

faqs.question: Is the Episcopal Palace the same as the Bishop's Palace in Porto?
faqs.answer: Yes. The Bishop's Palace of Porto is also called the Episcopal Palace, and in Portuguese it is the Paço Episcopal do Porto. It stands beside Porto Cathedral on the Terreiro da Sé.

faqs.question: What can you see inside the Bishop's Palace?
faqs.answer: The monumental neoclassical staircase, with mural painting and flowers carved in granite; palatial salons with portraits of the Bishops of Porto, including works by Henrique Medina and Júlio Resende; the recreated dining room of the 3rd Viscounts of São João da Pesqueira, with the “Baixela Manuelina” silver service; and views over the Douro at the end of the visit.

faqs.question: Can you combine the Bishop's Palace with Porto Cathedral?
faqs.answer: Yes. The palace adjoins Porto Cathedral on the Terreiro da Sé, so the two are easy to visit together. Ask at the desk about the combined ticket with the Cathedral.
